title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
why: A-type agentic manipulation harness: a generalist model commands manipulators directly via AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation, with an optional persistent memory store for cross-episode learning.

title: A Controlled Study of Models, Skills, Feedback, and Curriculum in Agentic Robotics
why: B-type controlled evaluation of the agentic-robotics self-learning loop: coding agents implement and iteratively improve robot policies from simulated and real-world physical interactions, isolating model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum.
mechanism: Controlled simulation study of coding-agent policy improvement spanning nine manipulation tasks, 631 experiment configurations, and 28K coding-agent rollouts. Factors varied independently: model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum. Analysis focuses on failure attribution, spatial/geometric reasoning, and selective code restructuring as the self-learning bottlenecks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): 9 manipulation tasks, 631 configurations, and 28K coding-agent rollouts; authors conclude the bottleneck is often interpreting available information into the right policy update rather than access to sufficient information (numeric tables beyond abstract unread).

title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
why: A-type embodied multi-agent harness built around code as a scaling interface: learned correction codes (corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, action proposals) supervise and adapt a VLA (A2-WLA), with a history-conditioned adapter for post-failure completion.
mechanism: A2-MEAS multi-agent framework: MetaBrain supplies training supervision and runtime guidance; a correction encoder/adapter absorb correction-code knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. A2-WLA adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a VLA; a history-conditioned adapter is used for post-failure recovery on long-horizon tasks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): A2-WLA reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction; A2-MEAS reaches 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success on all 100 public tasks; A2-WLA 93.98% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 (95.05% with the complete system); 12 real-robot household tasks 57.92% vs 26.67% for π0.5; in long-horizon pour-over coffee, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%.

title: HomeLoop: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot-IoT Coordination in Everyday Domestic Assistance and Safety
why: B-type Isaac Sim benchmark/framework for VLM-driven home-assistant robots that must coordinate with cameras, IoT devices, and wearables under ambiguous hazards, scored by a temporal-logic runtime monitor on outcomes and action costs.
mechanism: HomeLoop: Isaac Sim framework combining robot bodies, networked devices and wearables, simulated residents/visitors, faulty sensors, and time-evolving hazards. Benchmark has 20 tasks across five families designed so the same alert can have different causes. A runtime monitor applies temporal-logic checks to the final outcome and intermediate actions; each action carries a predefined cost.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): six open-weight and proprietary VLMs evaluated; best family-balanced score 61.9%; failed episodes involving prohibited interventions outnumber those involving missed required interventions by more than two to one (over-reaction, e.g. shutting off the stove before investigating). Release intended with 2,100 home layouts, five robot bodies, and 20 networked device types.

title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
why: A-type/B-type hybrid: an LLM (GPT-6 Astra) debugs a robot foundation policy by editing token-embedding weights through a CPU workspace and budgeted simulator feedback, without gradient updates or new demonstrations.
mechanism: Weight-space programming for robot foundation policies: GPT-6 Astra reads π0.5 weights and edits as few as 65 token-embedding rows using a CPU workspace and budgeted simulator feedback, with no gradient updates or new demonstrations. Controls include matched random-direction edits and full replacement using the editor's own lexicon; authors distinguish lexical instruction-grounding repair from general capability acquisition.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): three independent sessions on π0.5 all improve success on 765 held-out paraphrases; the best raises success from 86.3% to 92.0% (48 repairs, four regressions; exact paired p=1.31×10^{-10}). Among the 335 instructions containing edited tokens, success rises from 74.3% to 87.5%; the other 430 episodes have zero outcome changes. Across 13 further robot sessions the editor declines 12 candidates. Separately, benchmark metadata lowers FastWAM success from 70.0% to 48.6%, while the evaluated VLA's aggregate rate is unchanged.

title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
why: B-type benchmark of recursive self-improvement in which an improver revises the agent harness (prompts, tools, memory, control loop) on vision and robotics tasks under a fixed budget, isolating harness edits from solution-only improvement.
mechanism: Flex-RSI: each round an executor improves the task solution (kept only if it scores higher on held-out validation) and an improver then revises the harness, including the executor and itself. Every run starts from the same general-purpose harness; the final solution is scored on hidden test data. Tasks span perception, reasoning, robot action, 3D reconstruction, visual creation, and infrastructure.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): closed-source and open-weight models evaluated; self-improvement helps most when the agent builds its own solution; success/failure-only feedback holds back open-weight models; open-weight models fall furthest behind where outputs must pass strict physical-stability or exact-correctness checks; paired runs show that editing the harness itself contributes to the gains (numeric tables beyond abstract unread).

title: VLA Handover: Failure-Prediction-Based Switching from On-Robot to Server VLA Models
why: B-type execution-monitor / handoff layer: a small on-robot VLA runs by default and switches to a large server VLA only when failure is predicted, minimizing request cost under a required success probability without retraining either model.
mechanism: VLA handover: the robot runs a small S-VLA and switches to a server L-VLA only when the S-VLA is predicted to fail. Switching is posed as minimizing request cost subject to a required success probability; a heuristic framework is used because the problem cannot be solved directly, and neither VLA is retrained.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): SmolVLA and π0.5 on three of the four LIBERO suites — success rises 11–22 percentage points over the S-VLA alone, with 49–77% fewer server requests than server-only control at a 2–4 percentage-point lower success rate; completion time grew less with network latency.

title: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation
why: A-type skill-library / frozen-primitive composition for VLAs: reusable skills are stored as frozen low-rank action-expert adapters in a primitive bank and mixed at inference by a per-chunk VLM-conditioned router that tracks task progress.
mechanism: PRISM represents reusable skills as parameter-level primitives: each skill family is a dedicated low-rank action-expert adapter in a primitive bank, augmented with skill-specific low-rank residuals and composed at inference by a per-chunk VLM-conditioned router that reads the prefix representation to track progress. The router is supervised by per-chunk labels from a deterministic, task-conditioned, action-derived oracle. During composite training the primitives stay frozen so base per-skill adapters are preserved.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on RoboCasa365, PRISM achieves 56.43% atomic-skill success and 20.00% long-horizon composite-task success, vs 17.86% / 17.50% for a standard π0.5-LoRA two-stage fine-tune. Additional validation on an AgileX PIPER real-robot setup (detail unread).

title: VICTR: Value-Informed In-Context Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models
why: A-type in-context / retrieval harness for VLAs: an In-Context Value Function Estimator estimates task-relative progress against a reference demonstration and retrieves stage-aligned demo chunks for a π0.5 policy post-trained for in-context action generation.
mechanism: VICTR: IC-VFE conditions on a reference demonstration video, a language instruction, and the current observation to estimate task-relative progress, aligning the current state with a demonstrated execution even for tasks unseen in training. Estimated progress selects demonstration chunks at corresponding execution stages and supplies them to a π0.5 policy post-trained for in-context action generation.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on unseen out-of-domain real-world manipulation tasks, success rises from 6.2% for a fine-tuned π0.5 baseline to 23.8%, and task progress rate more than doubles from 28.9% to 55.5%.

title: HiMEM: Hippocampus-Inspired Memory Consolidation, Pruning, and Composition for Vision-Language-Action Models in 3D Scenes
why: A-type experience-memory harness for VLAs in 3D scenes: hippocampus-inspired consolidation of episodic memories into compact semantic memories, pruning of redundant episodes, and flexible composition of multiple memories at inference.
mechanism: HiMEM: (1) a memory-consolidation mechanism synthesizes extensive episodic experiences into a compact set of semantic memories; (2) an episodic pruning step removes memories whose contents are captured by those semantic memories; (3) a composition mechanism jointly uses multiple episodic and semantic memories for complex/cross-scenario tasks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): experiments on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus across different VLA backbones; improves the average success rate of π0 from 91.88% to 98.20% on LIBERO (other numeric tables unread).

title: Q-OIL: Optimistic Exploration in Learning from Human Interventions
why: A-type human-intervention / on-policy correction for robots and pretrained VLAs: a progress-based model of when humans intervene, plus Q-OIL, which adds optimistic bonuses to intervention transitions and softly guides exploration toward human corrections.
mechanism: A progress-based human-intervention model (humans tend to intervene when agent progress stalls; corrective actions are often suboptimal) is used for more realistic simulated-human benchmarking. Q-OIL adds optimistic bonuses to intervention transitions in RL and softly guides exploration toward human corrections; decoupled critics keep those bonuses from backing up to pre-intervention states.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): 10–50% higher success than competitive baselines in simulation and on real robots; improves pretrained VLAs on two bimanual manipulation tasks. The progress-based human model achieves higher rank correlation with real-user algorithm rankings than common simulated-human assumptions (exact correlation unread).

title: Localizing and Editing the Goal Representation of a Vision-Language-Action Model
why: B-type LLM-robot safety / runtime-monitor study: tests whether OpenVLA follows prohibition instructions ('do not X'), localizes the executed-goal representation, and evaluates activation patching, steering, and external goal monitors on LIBERO-Goal.
mechanism: Closed-loop rollouts combined with activation patching, linear probes, activation steering, and runtime monitors on OpenVLA / LIBERO-Goal. Measures whether negation changes the executed task; localizes where the goal is represented (instruction tokens before layer 12; last prompt token from layer 16 onward); tests fixed steering vectors and mid-rollout instruction changes.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): negation had no detectable effect on which task OpenVLA executed — the forbidden task ran in 79% of negated rollouts vs 78% completion of plain tasks. A layer-8 steering vector redirected 12 of 18 rollouts; fixed vectors and prefill patches at layers 12–20 redirected none of 158; from layer 16, only patches at every decoded action token redirected the robot (15 of 18 at layer 24). Authors recommend enforcing prohibitions outside the instruction and monitoring goal read-outs against the specification.
